Kennecott Land's West Bench plan calls for major development, including an urban center along I-80. Main Street has seen commercial decline and some vacant storefronts, though it was remodeled in 2006 and is a popular filming location.

The sources reviewed give no timeline or price effect for the West Bench plan, so a seller should compare recent nearby sales rather than assume it will change values.

The main east and west road is West 3500 South (SR-171), and the main north and south road is South 8400 West (SR-111). UTA route 35 runs along 3500 South every 15 minutes on weekdays and loops through Main Street, and the TRAX Green Line is nearby.

Magna is in the Granite School District. Elementary schools are Copper Hills, Elk Run, Lake Ridge, Magna and Pleasant Green. Matheson Junior High is the middle school, and Cyprus High School competes at the 5A level. Brockbank Junior High closed in 2016 and merged into the Cyprus High campus.

It provides planning and zoning, building permits and inspections, code enforcement and business licensing. It does not provide police, fire or sanitation.

The MSD code enforcement page lists the types of violations it handles:

  • Outdoor storage of junk
  • Parking on dirt or grass
  • More than two unregistered or inoperable vehicles on a property
  • Unpermitted signs, home businesses or short-term rentals
  • Exceeding the number of unrelated occupants
  • Setback violations, such as carports too close to a property line

Construction without a permit goes to the MSD Building Department at (385) 468-6688. Code enforcement is at 860 W Levoy Drive, Suite 300, Taylorsville, and the phone is (385) 910-5780. The page does not say when each rule was last changed, so owners should call to confirm.

Salt Lake County tax notices are mailed by November 1, taxes are due November 30, unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty rises after January 31. The Auditor sends the tax sale listing on March 15, and the final tax sale takes place on the fourth Thursday of May.

The Salt Lake County Recorder is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, Salt Lake City, and can be reached at 385-468-8145, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The county's Property Watch service sends alerts to help protect a property. Richard and Emily Hamblin settled the area in 1877 and called it Sand Ridge. The Utah Central Railroad crossed the area in 1869, and a canal that arrived in 1884 sparked a population jump. Clearfield became a town on July 17, 1922, and a city on March 21, 1946.

War changed the place. Hill Field began construction in 1940, and the Navy commissioned the Clearfield Naval Supply Depot on April 10, 1943, to supply the Pacific Fleet. The Navy phased the depot out in 1962, and private firms moved in. That site is now the Freeport Center.

How did Holladay start, and why does its history matter to a seller?

Holladay began in 1847, when pioneers from the Mississippi Company, including John Holladay of Alabama, reached the Salt Lake Valley and found a spring-fed stream they called Spring Creek near what is now Kentucky Avenue. A few men wintered in dugouts there, and the settlement took Holladay's name.

The area later went by Big Cottonwood and then Holladay-Cottonwood. The city was incorporated on November 29, 1999 as Holladay-Cottonwood. The name was shortened to Holladay on December 14, 1999. Holladay claims to be the oldest continuously inhabited settlement in Utah, a claim that rests on Salt Lake City being briefly abandoned in 1857.

Liquefaction is most likely in low central parts of a valley with shallow groundwater, so risk varies from one lot to the next. The survey also says the maps show only general patterns and that a site-specific study by a Utah-licensed engineer and geologist is needed for a particular lot.

Older masonry is the main concern. Unreinforced brick buildings from roughly the 1920s to the 1960s were not designed for sideways ground motion. Sellers of Holladay brick houses from that era should expect buyers to ask about bracing and chimney anchors.

Hector C. Haight wintered cattle in Farmington's grassy lowlands in 1847 and 1848, and five other families soon joined him. In 1852 the territorial legislature created Davis County and made the settlement, then called North Cottonwood, its county seat, renaming it Farmington.

Residents built Utah's first courthouse in 1854 and 1855, a two-story adobe building, and partly walled the town with mud. The Utah Central Railroad arrived in 1870, and the city incorporated on December 15, 1892 with 1,180 residents. Simon Bamberger developed the Lagoon resort in 1896, and it grew into Utah's largest amusement park.

The 2020 census counted 24,531 people, up from 18,275 in 2010. In 1990 the population was close to 10,000, so the city has more than doubled in about three decades.

Only the market value can be appealed, not the tax rate, and only the owner or an agent with a notarized authorization may file. Accepted evidence includes:

What is the weather like, and what does it do to a Hurricane house?

Hurricane has a desert climate with very hot summers. The closest long-term station is in St. George, where the average July high is about 101.9 degrees Fahrenheit and about 60 afternoons a year reach 100 degrees or higher. Annual precipitation runs roughly 9 inches.

Winters are mild during the day but can freeze overnight, with about 60 mornings a year at or below 32 degrees. The summer monsoon usually starts in mid-July and lasts into mid-September, bringing localized thunderstorms.

Heat of that kind is hard on roofing and cooling equipment, so a seller can expect questions about how old both are. Monsoon storms add a reason to look at drainage around the lot.

Water has made history here. The dike at Quail Creek, an offstream reservoir run by the Washington County Water Conservancy District, breached at 12:30 a.m. on January 1, 1989, draining about 25,000 acre-feet. Damage was put at about $12 million, and no lives were lost.

Which schools and utilities serve Hurricane?

The Washington County School District serves Hurricane. Hurricane High School teaches grades 10 to 12 and also draws students from La Verkin, Toquerville and Springdale, and the city has two elementary schools, an intermediate school for grades 6 and 7, a middle school for grades 8 and 9, and the charter school Valley Academy.

Hurricane runs its own electric utility. The American Public Power Association named Hurricane City Power a top-performing public power provider for 2024, the eighth national reliability award the utility has received, and the utility reported delivering power 99.9846% of the time. Fire protection comes through the Hurricane Valley Fire District, which the city's short-term rental rules reference.

The city offices are at 147 N 870 W, and the general number is 435-635-2811. The business license office is inside the Planning and Zoning Department, and a home-based business can be approved under Title 10, Chapter 42 of the city code.

What are Hurricane's short-term rental rules?

Hurricane requires a business license for any short-term rental, caps licenses in single-family zones, and does not allow another licensed rental within 300 feet. The rules are in Section 3-10-11 of the city code.

RuleHurricane requirement
License cap, single-family zonesThree licenses per 1,000 residents
SpacingNo other licensed rental within 300 feet
ParkingOne off-street space per bedroom
OccupancyTen, unless the fire district approves more with suppression
Complaint responseWithin one hour
FinesUp to $750 per violation, and each day counts

A license does not follow the house automatically. The buyer must apply for a new license within 45 days of purchase, or the license is forfeited, and the owner would have to reapply or join the waiting list. A seller who markets a house as a rental should tell the buyer this up front, because the license can be part of what an investor is paying for.

How do Washington County property tax dates work?

Washington County real property tax is due November 30 each year, even if no notice arrives. The Treasurer's office does not offer payment plans, though partial payments of $10 or more per parcel are accepted at any time.

  • Payments apply first to interest, then penalty, then tax, and with several delinquent years Utah law sends money to the most recent year first.
  • Each May, the Clerk-Auditor sells properties that have been delinquent for at least five years.
  • Utah does not allow the sale of tax liens or tax lien certificates.
  • If neighbors received a notice and you did not, call the Treasurer for a copy.

Taxes are a lien against the property, not the owner, and the title company prorates them when a house sells mid-year. The Treasurer is at 111 East Tabernacle St. in St. George, phone 435-301-7720.

Valuation appeals follow state law: the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor gives notice. A home that is a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value, and a buyer must file a new claim for the exemption after a sale.

What happens at closing for a Hurricane sale?

A Hurricane sale closes at a title company, and the deed is recorded with the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle in St. George. The Recorder does not accept recordings after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and its phone number is 435-301-7680.

State law requires a deed to name the grantees, give a mailing address for tax billing and carry a proper legal description. The signer's name needs to match the owner of record, which is worth checking early on an inherited house.

What do Hurricane sellers typically weigh?

Hurricane sellers choose between listing with an agent, selling on their own, or taking a cash offer. A listing means preparing the house for showings in a market with new construction nearby, while a cash sale lets the house sell as it is.

  • Empty houses that still carry tax, utility and insurance costs.
  • Short-term rentals that lost a license or fell short of the city rules.
  • Inherited houses with out-of-state heirs.
  • Older homes with aging roofs, evaporative coolers or failing air conditioning.

Ask any buyer for the closing date and proof of funds in writing, and compare the result against a listing's net after repairs and commission.

More questions about Hurricane, UT

What is Hurricane's population?

The Census Bureau counted 20,036 residents in 2020 and estimates 25,745 for July 1, 2025.

When is property tax due in Hurricane?

November 30 each year, billed by the Washington County Treasurer, even if you did not get a notice. The office offers no payment plans, though partial payments of $10 or more are accepted.

Does a short-term rental license transfer when I sell my Hurricane house?

No. The buyer must apply for a new license within 45 days of the purchase or the license is forfeited. The buyer could then face a waiting list.

Is Hurricane's climate hard on houses?

It can be. Nearby St. George averages a July high near 102 degrees and about 60 days a year at 100 or above, so roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes take heavy wear.

Where is a deed recorded for a Hurricane house?

At the Washington County Recorder's office in St. George. It does not accept recordings after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and the title company usually handles the filing.

Where is West Haven, Utah?

West Haven is a city in Weber County, about 35 miles north of Salt Lake City and west of the Wasatch Mountains. It borders Ogden to the east, Roy to the south, Hooper to the west and Marriott-Slaterville to the north.

The Weber and Ogden Rivers meet in the northeastern part of the city, and the elevation is about 4,269 feet. West Haven belongs to the Ogden-Clearfield metropolitan area, so many residents commute to jobs in Ogden, Roy and Davis County.

The city is young on paper and old on the map. It was incorporated on July 1, 1991, by combining the unincorporated communities of Kanesville and Wilson. The street grid, the farmhouses and the newer subdivisions all sit inside one set of city limits, which is why two West Haven houses can sell very differently.

How did Kanesville and Wilson become West Haven?

Both communities were farming settlements first. Wilson was formed in 1854 and named for four Wilson brothers who started farming there that year. John Martin moved from Ogden in 1856 and was the first to settle west of the Weber River, and an irrigation company formed in 1879.

Kanesville was first settled in 1868 as Northwest Hooper and was later named for Thomas L. Kane when a ward was organized in 1882. Kanesville Elementary still carries the old name.

The city installed a citywide sewer system in 2002, which opened the door to denser building. Wikipedia lists the population at 2,172 in 1990, 3,976 in 2000, 10,272 in 2010 and 16,739 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate quoted at the top of this page is 25,627.

Homeowner vacancy in 2020 was 0.7%, a very low figure that points to few empty houses in the city.

What do the seasons mean for a house near Ogden?

West Haven has four real seasons, with hot summers and cold winters. Climate normals for nearby Ogden show an average July high of 91.3 degrees and a January low of 21.2 degrees, with about 16.4 inches of precipitation a year.

Ogden's record low is minus 23 degrees and its record high is 106 degrees. Snow usually begins in late October or early November and ends around April.

That swing is hard on a few parts of a house:

  • Roofs and gutters that hold snow and ice.
  • Exposed pipes and sprinkler lines that can freeze.
  • Furnaces, which carry a heavy load for half the year.
  • Driveways and flatwork that crack as the ground freezes and thaws.

A buyer's inspector will check each of these, and a heating system near the end of its life is a frequent point of negotiation.

What is daily life like in West Haven?

West Haven is a fully urban city by the census definition, yet it keeps some farm character. The Kanesville Elementary profile describes mostly single-family neighborhoods, more condominiums and multifamily buildings being added, and 19th-century farmhouses and working farms that raise crops and animals.

The city bought 40 acres for a park in 1994, and the site has playground equipment, sports fields and a historical marker. Plans call for a River Parkway Trail with a fishing bridge and a pedestrian tunnel under 21st Street that would link to the Weber County Centennial Trail. City committees cover trails and parks, beautification and historic preservation, and the city runs its own arena and park reservations.

For a seller, that mix matters. A house near the new trails and schools reaches families, while a house on a larger rural lot reaches buyers who want space for animals or outbuildings.

Which schools serve West Haven?

West Haven is served by the Weber School District, which covers all of Weber County except Ogden City. Schools in or near the city include Country View Elementary, Haven Bay Elementary, Kanesville Elementary and West Haven Elementary.

Rocky Mountain Junior High and the newer Mountain View Junior High are in West Haven. Kanesville Elementary's feeder pattern runs to Rocky Mountain Junior High and then to Fremont High School in Plain City. Kanesville opened in 1977, and the district lists about 750 students there.

Two of the elementary and junior high buildings opened as recently as 2024, which tells you how fast the city has added families. Buyers with children often ask which school a house feeds, so confirm the boundary with the district before you advertise it.

What city rules and permits come up when selling in West Haven?

West Haven's Community Development group covers the Building Department, business licensing, code enforcement and emergency management. City offices are at 4150 S 3900 W, and the main line is 801-731-4519.

Ask the West Haven city office which permits apply before you start any repair work, and ask your title or escrow company what the buyer's lender will want to see.

Before you list, run through a short checklist:

  • Finished basements, decks or sheds should have permits on file.
  • Open code complaints should be cleared with city code enforcement.
  • Utility accounts, including the West Haven Special Service District bill, should be current.

How do property tax and recording work in Weber County?

Weber County bills property tax once a year and the payment is due November 30. The county's 2026 calendar shows tax notices mailed on October 17, valuation notices around July 20 and an appeal deadline of September 15. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and penalties and interest follow.

Utah gives a primary residence a 45% exemption, so tax applies to 55% of market value. In Weber County the home must be the occupant's main home for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a tenant's primary residence can qualify as well. Nightly rentals, vacation homes and second homes do not. If the county mails a declaration form and you do not return it within 30 days, the exemption is removed. Call the Assessor at (801) 399-8572 if you are unsure of your status.

Deeds are recorded at the Weber County Recorder, 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 370, Ogden. Fees changed on May 6, 2026: $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages, and $2.00 for each description over ten. Property tax is prorated by the title company at closing.

What are your options for selling a West Haven house?

West Haven owners can list with an agent, sell on their own or ask for a cash offer, and the right choice depends on the condition of the house and how much time you have. The condition of the house, the roof and the heating system usually drive what a buyer will pay.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Utah as they stand. Owners who contact us usually have a reason to move quickly, such as a job change, an inherited house, a tenant they want to be done with or a mortgage they are behind on. We look at the property and explain what a sale would involve, and you choose whether to go ahead.

What do West Haven sellers often face?

  • Competition from newly built houses in a city that has grown by tens of percent in a few years.
  • Older farmhouses and rural lots where the land and the house are valued differently.
  • Primary residence exemption questions when a house is converted to a rental.
  • Out-of-state heirs who need to sort out a deed and a recording before anything else.

More questions about West Haven, UT

What county is West Haven, UT in?

West Haven is in Weber County. Property tax, deeds and valuation appeals all go through Weber County offices in Ogden.

When is property tax due in West Haven?

Weber County's due date is November 30. Unpaid taxes are delinquent on December 1, and the county's calendar shows interest beginning February 1 on the prior year's delinquent balance.

What does it cost to record a deed in Weber County?

The Recorder lists $45.00 for the first page, with no charge for additional standard pages and $2.00 for each legal description over ten, effective May 6, 2026.

Which school district covers West Haven?

The Weber School District serves West Haven. Elementary schools nearby include Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven Elementary, with Rocky Mountain and Mountain View junior highs.

Can I sell a West Haven house as-is?

Yes. You are not required to fix a house before selling it, and a cash sale to a buyer who takes the property in its present condition is one way to skip repairs.
